lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.29 - A Listen. Then act it out.

details: Listen. Then act it out checks understanding of language and vocabulary in a story using visuals as an aid. Then students practise speaking by acting out the story.
Look for students carefully listening to the story and engaging with the visuals, then correct imitation of the pronunciation and intonation of the story lines, with appropriate gesture.
“I’ve got a pet tiger! He’s soft and cuddly and sleeps on my bed every night! What animal does Amy have? Shall we find out where he is?“

Heads Up (Reading): 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and help Ss to understand the text by asking questions, practicing skimming (reading for gist), scanning (reading for specific information) and detail (reading for comprehension). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down (Listen and Follow): 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together (Video, then act it out): 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.29 - B. Look and choose

details: Look and choose tests students’ understanding of the story through multiple choice questions about scenes from the story.
Look for correct answers  and neat circling in students’ books.
“My tiger likes scaring other animals. Can you help me name some animals that might be scared of him?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.83 - A Read and number

details: Read and number checks students’ understanding of a similar story by reading short dialogues and ordering the pictures.
Look for correct numbering and neat writing of numbers.
“I’m sad for my tiger that he does’t have any friends. All the other animals hide from him.”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.30 - C Make your own story

details: Make your own story gives students the opportunity to personalise a story by circling words and using stickers. Then they practise speaking by telling the story.
Look for accurate word choices and sticker placement inside the story pictures. Also correct pronunciation and authentic intonation when students tell their stories.
“I’m going to put my tiger in this story! Can you create your own story?”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.30 - Tongue Twisters Listen and say

details: Listen and say practises the pronunciation of words with /h/ and /w/ at sentence level.
Look for clear pronunciation of words in the sentences and confident repetition.
“Did you guess my tiger is a soft toy? He’s not really scary at all! What about these animals?”
